summary: Feed s151_double to NDR is degraded: 8.9% duplicate packets and 2.0% TCP packet loss detected. Both faults reduce NDR detection coverage - duplicates waste capacity and skew analytics, drops break stream reassembly and full payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: 8.9% duplicates (168/1885) indicates overlapping ingress feeds (e.g., both sides of a TAP pair or overlapping SPANs aggregated) delivered to the NDR without packet broker deduplication.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes cycles processing same packet twice, inflates flow/byte counts, can cause false positives and inaccurate analytics, and unnecessarily consumes 10G tool port bandwidth despite needing full payload and both directions.

recommended_fix.why: Enable hardware deduplication on the packet broker for this feed to suppress identical packets within a short window before egress to the NDR, preserving bidirectional visibility while eliminating double-counting.

findings.root_cause: 2.0% TCP gaps (36/1845 packets with missing data) indicates loss between capture point and NDR, likely packet broker egress buffer exhaustion/microburst drops or oversubscribed SPAN. Tool overload is healthy, so loss is in the visibility fabric, not the NDR itself.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot reassemble TCP streams with missing segments, breaking full payload inspection, file extraction, and signature matching - directly reduces detection coverage for attacks that span multiple packets.

recommended_fix.why: Use packet broker aggregation with deep, flow-aware buffering on the egress to the 10G NDR port to absorb microbursts and prevent random drops, ensuring complete TCP streams for full payload analysis.
